tagline: Gravel under the east wall of Steens Mountain, down to Fields.
intro: OR 78 leaves Burns to the southeast past Lawen and Crane, and near milepost 65 the route turns off onto East Steens Road. There the gravel starts. It runs south past the sagebrush of the Sheepshead Mountains and a string of small lakes named Five Cent, Ten Cent and Fifteen Cent, which go dry in some years.

Then Steens Mountain comes into view, a single fault-block mountain rising a vertical mile above the Alvord Basin. It keeps the west side of the road from there on, with the salt flats of the Alvord Desert to the east.
season: TripCheck gives spring through fall as the best time, though it calls the route enjoyable year round.

moments.title: Crane
moments.text: Until the railroad went on to Burns in 1924, Crane shipped livestock and kept four hotels, five restaurants and a dance hall, and after fires through 1938 it never got back.

moments.title: Alvord Desert
moments.text: Streams run onto this dry lake at the foot of the mountain and have no way out, so the water evaporates and leaves its salt on the playa.

moments.title: Fields
moments.text: Charles Fields homesteaded here in 1881 and built a stone roadhouse for the Winnemucca to Burns stage, since remodeled into a store and restaurant and still in use.

practical: East Steens Road is gravel but passable for regular passenger cars.
